The distinguishing criterion against the cured sibling is real: elf-b14-003's repair_note records that q2 there was 'cured by redesign rather than argued away' because its distractors self-destructed on form, and no equivalent self-destruct exists in q1 or q2 here. The round-2 leg concedes this is 'A near-structural pattern' and the original leg put the blind pick at ~82%, the highest confidence anywhere in the unit. The clause tested belongs to an invented 1798 ordinance for an invented parish, so no real-world source supplies the answer. The adjudication's further point — that curing q1 is self-defeating because its key IS the institution's defining fact — is correct, and for the actual construct (a Swedish 18-year-old reading for comprehension, with stycke 1 defining sockenmagasin from zero) both items are genuine reading questions.

findings.claim: Bjärnhult's explicitly deferred rename recommendation survived a dedicated real-entity rename campaign and two repair rounds that both touched this unit, and it survives the 2026-08-25 fix round as well.
findings.evidence: Sweep verdict: 'near ... Real bearer in the same broad domain (Swedish rural local history), but the mismatch of settlement type and the absence of any real magazine record keep this below the blocking bar. Worth a rename if the batch is being touched anyway.' Independently re-confirmed: Bjärnhult (Äsphults Bjärnhult) is an ort in Äsphults socken, Kristianstads kommun, Skåne, 8 inhabitants in 2009, originally a single-farm village known since the 1600s, with a second Bjärnhult nearer Kristianstad, plus Bjärnhult/Björnhult herrgård in Stafsinge socken, Halland. The unit attaches an invented 1832 sockenstämmoprotokoll and an invented kyrkvärd to the name. Since that recommendation, commit 4681b85 ran a 'real-entity rename campaign — 10 units repaired', two repair rounds touched this unit, the 2026-08-25 language pass changed this unit's byline given name for a law-13 reason, and the 2026-08-25 register fix round touched both the register entry and the unit's metadata — and Bjärnhult was not renamed in any of them.
findings.why: Not a REFUTE, and correctly not force-closed by the fix round, which re-recorded it as STILL OPEN rather than absorbing it — the right handling. The blocking bar requires a real bearer of the same type in the same domain carrying the fabrication, and real Bjärnhult is a hamlet inside a different, real parish, never a parish with a sockenstämma; the passage's parishes are framed as sitting in Hässle härad, which does not exist, so a reader cannot map the invented 1798 ordinance or 1832 protocol onto any real record. Recorded because the deferral condition ('if the batch is being touched anyway') has now been met five times and the decision has never been re-taken.
findings.fix: none applied — remains an open batch-level decision for the orchestrator.

entities.name: Hässle härad
entities.role_in_unit: invented district; its magazines were built under pressure from landshövding and präst, and its closure list is the evidence that undercuts Grimlund's savings-bank thesis
entities.detail: No härad of this name has existed. Sweden held 226 härader in 1970 and 'Hässle' is not among them; the real bearers of the string are Hässle, a manor/gård in Fittja socken, Enköpings kommun, Uppland (site of the 1869 Hessle meteorite), and Hassle socken in Vadsbo härad, Västergötland — a different spelling and a different entity type.
